exact_missing_items: Make the owner-doc distinction explicit: inspection/provenance refs stay in event and record payloads; route/open contracts own navigation identity.
Keep detail_ref, report_ref, evidence_ref, usage_event_ref, workflow_refs, docker_refs, kubernetes_refs as record/provenance families, not route payload surrogates.
Keep resume_url only as serialized transport derived from canonical route identity.
This split will make the owner-doc rewrite much easier because most refs do not need replacement. The real conflict sits almost entirely on resume_url, not on the broader *_ref family.
Navigation should follow the same pattern instead of claiming a hard flag day.

existing user-facing wrapper commands may remain; their payload semantics should normalize through `route_target` / `OpenSubject`; older payload shapes can be accepted during migration; new producers/docs should emit the canonical normalized target model
new docs/producers MUST prefer canonical route-target forms; consumers MAY accept older wrapper-local payloads during migration; migration aliases MUST NOT become permanent parallel canon
Reuse the event-alias and recovery-command migration style as the template for navigation normalization.
Projection closure for route payloads: every primary_route_payload on an attention item and every resume_url must be derivable from the canonical route payload schema
Any surface that accepts a route payload as input (deep-link, cmd.*.open_in_*, palette action, attention item navigation) must validate it against the canonical schema
Stale or malformed route payloads must surface a clear user-facing error, not silently navigate to the wrong surface
Projection freshness model: event-driven updates are primary; each projection must carry one of these health states: current, refreshing, stale, failed

Promotion gates must be defined at three levels: lane_to_package = local correctness + uncontaminated lane + required automated verification; package_to_seam_available = trusted baseline + package evidence + acceptable overseer verdict; seam_complete = integration review + no unresolved major/critical findings + seam evidence + no pending corroboration/remediation
Publish a single superseding canonical payload block in Contracts_V0.md for scheduler/safe-point/remediation records and explicitly demote older variants
Add a canonical actor envelope shared by runtime records, provider-account snapshots, receipts, Usage pivots, and conversational actor telemetry
Normalize cross-surface receipt records so project_id, actor refs, created_at_utc, and usage_event_ref are required whenever a surface may pivot historically or across projects
Define usage_event_ref once as a locator-grade canonical reference and reuse it everywhere rather than inventing a new opaque ID family
Normalize Run Graph onto canonical cmd.runtime.* / cmd.orchestrator.open_in_* command bindings, add the missing action envelope, and add trust-state gating rules
Allow short-term concern rendering to piggyback on finding_refs[], but define a minimal non-remediation node_concerns[] projection next
Pre-attempt blocked episodes still need blocked_sequence handling without fabricating attempt_id
usage_event_ref should be a structured locator, not just a display string
Reconciliation-readiness criteria must be specified: when is a project/run state ready for reconciliation after an account switch or degradation event?

Criteria list must be explicit and testable: all pending receipts committed, no open HITL requests tied to the old account context, permission snapshots revalidated under new account, active workers notified and acknowledged
This criteria list is the gate for resuming execution and must be normative in Contracts_V0.md and referenced by Multi-Account.md
Requirements-doc-builder flow: collaborative ideation → structured questioning → requirements documents; this is a defined workflow with a structured output
Seam review outputs must include: verdict, failure classes with severity, evidence bundle/rationale, remediation-node or graph-patch recommendation, corroboration requirement and outcome
The canonical actor envelope (project_id + actor_kind + sparse actor refs + requested/effective identity block) must be anchored in Contracts_V0.md
All runtime records, receipts, usage events, stream events, concern records, and attention items must reference the canonical actor envelope by name rather than redeclaring fields ad-hoc
actor_kind and execution_role enums must be defined in the same anchoring section
gap_candidates.blocking_reason: Concrete Plans/** document requires content reconciliation vs transfer obligation.
